outcome: No proof, disproof or AI-attributed resolution of Vojta's height-proximity conjecture was found in any source dated after 26 January 2024. Since then there are partial results on special cases and analogues (2024 to 2026), a conditional function-field and complex-analytic analogue, and one claimed Vojta-type inequality (arXiv:2403.10430, Joshi, March 2024) for the Legendre curve, restricted to bounded-degree points, which rests on the disputed Mochizuki inter-universal Teichmuller programme and has no independent verification found.
problem_asks: Read from the Wikipedia January 2024 wording (Vojta's conjecture on heights of points on algebraic varieties over algebraic number fields), the bullet asks for the following. (a) The main Vojta height inequality: for a number field K, a nonsingular projective variety X over K, an effective divisor D with simple normal crossings, an ample divisor H, a canonical divisor K_X, and a finite set S of places of K, the sum over v in S of the local height terms lambda_{D,v}(P), plus the height h_{K_X}(P), is bounded above by epsilon times h_H(P) plus a constant C_epsilon, for every epsilon > 0. (b) The inequality is asked to hold for all points P in X(K-bar) outside some proper Zariski-closed subset U, where U may depend on epsilon. (c) The bullet's own wording, 'heights of points on algebraic varieties over algebraic number fields', does not say whether points of unbounded degree are included; the Wikipedia article states the conjecture for points over a fixed number field K. (d) The bullet does not ask for the consequences (the abc conjecture, the Bombieri-Lang conjecture, Mordell-type finiteness, non-density of S-integral points), but the article lists these as what the conjecture implies. Known special cases, not asked for: curves via Roth, Siegel and Faltings; abelian varieties via Faltings (Wikipedia, as fetched).

events.what_happened: Kirti Joshi posted arXiv:2403.10430, 'Construction of Arithmetic Teichmuller Spaces IV: Proof of the abc-conjecture' (math.AG, cross-listed math.NT). v1 was submitted 15 March 2024 (97 KB). v2, revised 24 February 2025 (135 KB, 80 pages), states in its comments field that it is an expanded and revised edition of the March 2024 submission and that it 'fixes the issues with the previous version'. The abstract (as fetched) says that the theory, 'using Shinichi Mochizuki's rubric, leads to a proof' of the abc-conjecture, 'as asserted by Mochizuki'. Reading the v2 HTML (first 100,000 of 231,777 characters), section 1.4 says Theorem 7.1.1 (Corollary 2.3 of Mochizuki 2021d) 'Provides the main result (Vojta's Inequality)'. Section 1.5 says the main theorem, 'i.e. the Vojta Inequality', is 'established here in' Theorem 7.1.1; the table of contents lists section 7 as 'Vojta's Inequality for U_X(Q-bar)^{<=d}' and section 2.5 as 'Vojta's Height Inequality'. The body of section 7 was not in the text I read. The setting the visible text fixes is the Legendre family, U = (P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}) over Q-bar, its subset U_d of points of degree at most d, and compactly bounded subsets Z of U_d. The text says the inequality reduces abc via Mochizuki's reduction, and cites van Frankenhuysen (2002) for the equivalence of abc with Vojta's Inequality in this setting.
events.delivers: As the author claims it (the claim is not checked here): a Vojta-type height inequality in Mochizuki's normalisation for the curve U = P^1 minus three points over Q-bar, restricted to points of degree at most d, on compactly bounded subsets Z of U_d; together with the cited equivalence, this yields the abc conjecture. Restrictions: a single curve (the Legendre family), bounded-degree points, compactly bounded Z. No statement for general X, general D, general S, or unbounded degree appears in the text I read.
events.remains: The general height-proximity inequality for arbitrary smooth projective X over K, arbitrary normal-crossings D, arbitrary finite S and every epsilon > 0, with an exceptional set U that is proper and Zariski-closed; any points of unbounded degree; and any variety other than the Legendre curve. Whether the claimed inequality is a special case of the stated conjecture is the judging pass's call, but the restrictions above are what the text supports.
events.revisions: v1 15 Mar 2024 (97 KB); v2 24 Feb 2025 (135 KB, 80 pages, 'expanded and revised', 'fixes the issues with the previous version' per comments field). A later self-report, arXiv:2505.10568 (29 Apr 2025), is listed under disputes.
events.time_since_posted: about 31 months from v1 (March 2024 to October 2026); about 20 months from v2
events.doubts: (1) The underlying framework is Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmuller theory. Scholze and Stix (2018, 'Why abc is still a conjecture') located a gap in the step from Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 of IUT III and argued that small modifications will not rescue the proof strategy (quoted via search snippet; the PDF was not opened). Joshi's paper is an attempt to repair and defend that framework; the Vojta inequality it asserts is derived through Mochizuki's reduction (per the text read). (2) The author is a defender of the framework and says so: his own final report (arXiv:2505.10568) says every assertion of Scholze and Stix is 'mathematically false' while also holding that Mochizuki's proof is incomplete (per a secondary summary; not opened). (3) A July 2026 interim Lean-formalisation report by the LANA project reportedly found an unresolved compatibility problem at the same Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 step and gives no final verdict (search snippets and press coverage only; the PDF was unreadable to the fetch tool). (4) Mochizuki's own March 2024 report on Joshi's series exists (kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp), but its text was unreadable here, so I cannot say what it concludes. (5) The author states, without independent confirmation, that arXiv moderators placed the paper on hold. (6) I found no independent mathematician publicly engaging with the Vojta-inequality claim in particular; public discussion is about the abc consequence and the IUT dispute generally.
events.direction: Asserts a Vojta-type height inequality in the Legendre-curve, bounded-degree, compactly bounded setting, which is the direction Vojta's conjecture predicts. It claims the abc conjecture as a consequence. It does not claim a counterexample to anything the bullet asks, and it does not claim the general inequality.
people: Shinichi Mochizuki (originator of the underlying framework and of the cited Vojta inequality; not an independent reader)

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.10430v2 (first 100,000 of 231,777 characters read; acknowledgements not reached)
https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Report on a certain series of preprints (2024-03).pdf (tried; binary PDF, unreadable)

events.what_happened: Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmuller series asserts a Vojta height inequality for compactly bounded subsets of U_d (points of bounded degree on the Legendre curve), and deduces abc from it, via a reduction he attributes to his 2010 paper. Joshi's 2024 paper cites the assertion as 'Mochizuki 2021d, Corollary 2.3'. I did not open Mochizuki's IUT papers; the citation and the date are taken from Joshi's paper and from a secondary summary, which says the underlying papers date to 2021.
events.delivers: As claimed by Mochizuki and relied on by Joshi: a Vojta-type inequality in the Legendre-curve setting for compactly bounded sets, implying abc. Not verified here.
events.remains: Same as joshi-2024-03: the general Vojta height-proximity inequality for arbitrary varieties and divisors.
events.revisions: Not established. The 2021 date is the publication year cited by Joshi; the first posting date of the IUT papers was not verified.

checked_by.qualification: Arithmetic geometers; Scholze is a Fields medallist
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote 'Why abc is still a conjecture' after a week of discussion at RIMS, Kyoto. They concluded there is no proof and located a gap in the step from Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 of IUT III, which they said small modifications will not rescue (quoted via search snippet; not opened). This objection targets the abc route; it is not a reading of the Vojta-inequality claim in particular.

events.time_since_posted: about 5 years (2021 to 2026), counting from the publication year
events.doubts: The Scholze and Stix objection (2018) is to the framework this claim depends on, as described in joshi-2024-03. The LANA interim report (July 2026) reports a further unresolved compatibility issue at the same step (secondary sources only). Mochizuki's own later reports and Joshi's replies dispute these objections; see disputes.
events.direction: Asserts a Vojta-type inequality in the Legendre-curve, bounded-degree, compactly bounded setting, implying abc. The same direction as joshi-2024-03, from the same framework.

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.10430v2 (cites the 2021 work; the 2021 papers themselves were not opened)

events.what_happened: Mochizuki, Fesenko, Hoshi, Minamide and Porowski, 'Explicit estimates in inter-universal Teichmuller theory', Kodai Mathematical Journal 45(2) (2022), 175-236. Per a search snippet of the abstract (the PDF I opened was unreadable), the paper states that Mochizuki 'verified various numerically non-effective versions of the Vojta, ABC, and Szpiro Conjectures over number fields' and obtains numerically effective versions; its main consequence is an effective ABC inequality over mono-complex fields (Q or imaginary quadratic fields).
events.delivers: As the authors state it: numerically effective versions of Mochizuki's claimed non-effective Vojta-type, ABC and Szpiro statements over mono-complex fields, under the IUT framework. Restricted to number fields of mono-complex type for the effective abc statement. It does not state the general Vojta conjecture.
events.remains: The general Vojta height-proximity inequality over arbitrary number fields and varieties, and an effective (numerically) general statement.
events.revisions: Journal year 2022 found. The first preprint date was not established; the arXiv posting was not located.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (journal listing found; referee reports not available). Its acceptance is disputed by a separate line in the sources (RIMS reportedly said Mochizuki's IUT papers had not been accepted by a journal).

events.time_since_posted: about 4 years since the 2022 publication year
events.doubts: Rests on the IUT framework, which is disputed (see joshi-2024-03 and the disputes section). Within this line, the 'verified non-effective' claim is Mochizuki's and is not independently checked here. Journal acceptance of the IUT line is itself disputed in secondary sources.
events.direction: Claims the Vojta-type statements over number fields hold in a non-effective form and gives effective versions. In the direction the conjecture predicts, but as a claim within the disputed framework.

sources: Abstract as quoted in a search snippet; no AI mention seen in the snippet. The PDF was unreadable to the fetch tool, so the full text was not checked.

events.what_happened: Zhong-Peng Zhou, arXiv:2503.14510, 'The inter-universal Teichmuller theory and new Diophantine results over the rational numbers. I' (math.NT), submitted 8 March 2025. Applies IUT and a modified version over Q to prove an effective abc-type inequality for log|abc| >= 700, reducing the effective abc constant from 1.7 x 10^30 to 400, and gives Fermat-type bounds for x^r + y^s = z^t.
events.delivers: Effective abc-type bounds over Q, under IUT. Does not mention Vojta's conjecture.
events.remains: All of the bullet, since the result is about abc and the generalised Fermat equation.
events.revisions: v1 8 March 2025 only as far as the fetched page shows.
events.doubts: Relies on IUT, the disputed framework described under joshi-2024-03.
events.direction: Effective abc-type bounds, which are a consequence of Vojta's conjecture rather than the conjecture; direction not relevant to the stated inequality.

events.what_happened: Pagdame Tiebekabe, arXiv:2509.05300, 'Generalized Diophantine Approximation on Higher-Dimensional Varieties' (listed primary math.GM on the arXiv page). v1 submitted 18 August 2025, v2 revised 10 September 2025. The abstract (as fetched) claims new uniform height inequalities for rational points outside a sufficiently positive divisor, a locus where bounds may fail (Theorem 4.10), finiteness of S-integral points on log-general-type varieties, and says the framework 'naturally leads to Vojta-type inequalities in higher dimension', offered as 'new evidence toward Vojta's conjectures'. A third-party summary (Emergent Mind, opened) states that Section 6.1 presents a weak height-proximity form of Vojta's conjecture, that the unconditional output is a gap inequality m_S(P,D) <= (1 - epsilon) h_L(P) + C when tau(L;D) > 1, and that the paper gives partial progress when K_X + D is big. I did not open Section 6.1 of the paper itself.
events.delivers: As the abstract and the Emergent Mind summary indicate: unconditional height bounds for rational points outside a sufficiently positive divisor, and a 'gap' inequality under a positivity hypothesis (tau(L;D) > 1). Restricted to positive or big situations. The abstract claims no proof of the general statement.
events.remains: The height-proximity inequality with (1 + epsilon) for arbitrary X, D and S, without positivity, and off a proper closed set; the general case of the Wikipedia statement.
events.doubts: Single author, with the primary arXiv category listed as math.GM (General Mathematics), which is a metadata fact rather than a verdict; no referee record, journal publication or expert reading found. The 'gap inequality' is characterised only through a third-party summary; Section 6.1 and Theorem 4.10 were not read.
events.direction: Partial progress toward the height-proximity inequality, in the direction the conjecture predicts, under a positivity hypothesis. Does not claim the general statement.

events.what_happened: Nathan Grieve and Chatchai Noytaptim, arXiv:2504.09825, 'On relative fields of definition for log pairs, Vojta's height inequalities and asymptotic coordinate size dynamics', submitted 14 April 2025. The abstract (as fetched) formulates new conjectural Vojta-type height inequalities for log canonical pairs over finite extensions of number fields, introduces log resolutions relative to such extensions, and uses these for asymptotic coordinate size dynamics. The arXiv page as fetched says the paper is accepted by the Taiwanese Journal of Mathematics; I did not verify this.
events.delivers: Nothing proven about Vojta's conjecture for number fields. Conjectural formulation for log canonical pairs, over finite extensions.
events.remains: All of the bullet. The paper is a conjecture formulation, not a result on the stated problem.
events.revisions: v1 only, as far as the fetched page shows.
events.direction: Conjectural variant of Vojta-type inequalities for log canonical pairs over extensions; it proves nothing in the direction the stated conjecture predicts or against it.

events.what_happened: Brian Lehmann, David McKinnon and Matthew Satriano, arXiv:2403.02480, 'Approximating rational points on surfaces', submitted 4 March 2024 (math.AG, cross-listed math.NT). The abstract (as fetched) gives a strategy for deducing a slightly weaker form of a McKinnon conjecture on best rational approximations from Vojta's conjecture, and carries the strategy out to prove the full McKinnon conjecture for split surfaces. The fetched abstract does not say whether the split-surface result is conditional on Vojta's conjecture; a search snippet describes it as contingent on Vojta's conjecture. The body was not read.
events.delivers: A conditional implication from Vojta's conjecture to a weaker McKinnon approximation statement; the split-surface result is, per the snippet, contingent on Vojta. Unconditional content not established from the abstract.
events.remains: The Vojta conjecture itself is not settled; the paper's conclusions are about a different approximation statement.
events.revisions: v1 only, as far as the fetched page shows.
events.direction: Conditional on Vojta's conjecture, for a different approximation statement. Does not change what the bullet asks.

events.what_happened: Carlo Gasbarri, Ji Guo and Julie Tzu-Yueh Wang, arXiv:2401.13186, 'Campana conjecture for coverings of toric varieties over function fields'. v1 submitted 24 January 2024 (two days before the 26 January 2024 freeze); v2 3 November 2025. The abstract (as fetched) proves Vojta's abc conjecture over function fields for Campana points on projective toric varieties with high-multiplicity boundary, and derives a Campana-type statement for finite coverings.
events.delivers: A function-field analogue: Vojta's abc statement for Campana points on projective toric varieties over function fields, with high multiplicity. Not over number fields.
events.remains: The number-field statement of the bullet, entirely.
events.direction: Proves a function-field analogue of a Vojta abc statement, in the direction the conjectures predict. The analogue does not settle the number-field statement.

events.what_happened: Min Ru and Julie Tzu-Yueh Wang, arXiv:2410.19395, 'Vojta's abc conjecture for entire curves in toric varieties highly ramified over the boundary' (math.CV). v1 submitted 25 October 2024; v2 revised 10 February 2026. The abstract (as fetched) proves Vojta's abc conjecture for complex projective space P^n(C), under the hypothesis that entire curves in P^n(C) are highly ramified over the coordinate hyperplanes, and explores toric analogues; the n = 2 case extends Ji and Wang.
events.delivers: A complex-analytic (Nevanlinna-side) analogue of Vojta's abc statement, conditional on a hypothesis about entire curves. Not arithmetic.
events.doubts: Conditional on a hypothesis about entire curves; the v2 revision date is reported as current.
events.direction: A complex analogue, conditional on a hypothesis. In the direction Vojta's framework predicts, but it is not the arithmetic statement.

events.what_happened: Ryan C. Chen, Natalia Garcia-Fritz, Siddharth Mathur and Hector Pasten, arXiv:2602.06956, 'Towards Lang-Vojta via Degeneration', submitted 6 February 2026 (math.NT, math.AG). The abstract page (as fetched) proves finiteness and Zariski degeneracy of S-integral points on varieties over number fields in many cases with geometrically irreducible boundary divisors, gives explicit plane divisors (duals of smooth plane curves of degree at least 3), and answers a question of Achenjang and Morrow.
events.delivers: Finiteness of S-integral points (the integral-point, Lang-Vojta form) in the listed cases. The height-proximity inequality is not treated.
events.remains: The height-proximity inequality of the bullet, for all X, D and S; the general Lang-Vojta statement.
events.revisions: v1 only, as far as the abstract page shows.
events.direction: Partial progress toward the integral-point (Lang-Vojta) form, which is a sibling of the height-proximity inequality; in the direction the conjectures predict for the cases treated.

sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06956 (abstract page only; the acknowledgements and PDF were not opened)

events.what_happened: Xinyi Yuan, arXiv:2508.11888, 'On Vojta's proof of the Mordell conjecture', submitted 16 August 2025, revised 10 November 2025 (math.NT, math.AG). The abstract (as fetched) reorganises Vojta's Arakelov-geometry proof of Faltings' theorem (the Mordell conjecture), replacing the arithmetic Riemann-Roch theorem with Yuan's arithmetic Siu inequality.
events.delivers: Nothing on Vojta's conjecture. It reorganises an existing proof of a known theorem (Mordell-Faltings).
events.direction: Not about the stated conjecture; a method paper on a proven theorem.

events.what_happened: Jackson S. Morrow and Paul Vojta, arXiv:2502.10379, 'The non-Archimedean Green-Griffiths-Lang-Vojta conjecture for commutative algebraic groups with unipotent rank 1', submitted 14 February 2025 (math.AG, math.NT). The abstract (as fetched) works over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, proves the strong form of the non-Archimedean GGLV conjecture for subvarieties of commutative algebraic groups with linear part G_a x G_m^t, and identifies Kawamata and Lang-like exceptional loci.
events.delivers: A non-Archimedean function-field-type analogue of the Green-Griffiths-Lang-Vojta statement, for commutative algebraic groups of the stated type. Not over number fields.
events.remains: The number-field statement of the bullet, entirely.
events.revisions: v1 only, as far as the fetched page shows.
events.direction: An analogue in a different arithmetic setting; does not bear on the number-field statement.

events.what_happened: Guoquan Gao, arXiv:2511.17010, 'A counting argument for the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture on ramified covers of abelian varieties'. v1 submitted 21 November 2025 (first titled 'A complete proof of the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture for ramified covers of abelian varieties'); v2 revised 2 March 2026. The abstract (as fetched) proves the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture for projective varieties with finite maps to abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0, dropping the hyperbolicity or non-isotriviality assumption of Xie-Yuan.
events.delivers: The geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture, over function fields of characteristic 0, for varieties with finite maps to abelian varieties. Bombieri-Lang is a consequence of Vojta's conjecture, but the paper does not mention Vojta and is a different (geometric, function-field) statement.
events.remains: The Vojta height-proximity inequality, which is not addressed.
events.revisions: v1 21 Nov 2025 ('A complete proof of ...'); v2 2 Mar 2026 (current title).
events.doubts: The v1 title claimed a complete proof; v2 changed the title. The body was not read, so I have not checked the revision's content.
events.direction: A neighbouring conjecture (geometric Bombieri-Lang, a consequence of Vojta) proved in a restricted class over function fields. It does not address the stated height inequality.

sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17010 (abstract and version history only; body and acknowledgements not read)

events.what_happened: Junyi Xie and Xinyi Yuan, arXiv:2305.14789, first posted May 2023 (v1 title 'Partial Heights and the Geometric Bombieri-Lang Conjecture'; later title 'Partial Heights, Entire Curves, and the Geometric Bombieri-Lang Conjecture'). Published in Acta Mathematica 236 (2026), 365-416 (DOI 10.4310/ACTA.2026.v236.n2.a2, from a search snippet). A Peking University notice dated 30 July 2026 (opened) says the paper is published online in Acta Mathematica and proves the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture for finite hyperbolic ramified covers of abelian varieties, conditional in general on a non-degeneracy conjecture for partial heights.
events.delivers: The geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture for finite hyperbolic ramified covers of abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0; conditional on a partial-height non-degeneracy conjecture in general.
events.remains: The Vojta height-proximity inequality, which the paper does not address.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 May 2023; v2 retitled; Acta Mathematica 2026 (published online per the notice).
events.direction: A neighbouring Bombieri-Lang result, not the Vojta inequality; partially conditional in general and unconditional only in a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Aaron Levin, arXiv:1011.6561, 'The exceptional set in Vojta's conjecture for algebraic points of bounded degree', submitted 30 November 2010. The abstract (as fetched) uses certain elliptic surfaces to answer negatively the frequently raised question whether Vojta's conjecture holds when extended to all algebraic points, without a bound on degree.
events.delivers: A counterexample to the unbounded-degree version of Vojta's conjecture (all algebraic points, no degree bound). It leaves the fixed-number-field, bounded-degree statements intact as far as the abstract says.
events.remains: Not applicable to the bullet as worded (points over a fixed number field); it bears on any reading of 'algebraic points' that drops the bounded-degree condition.
events.revisions: v1 30 Nov 2010 as far as the page shows.
events.direction: Cuts against a variant (unbounded-degree algebraic points), not against the stated bullet. Discounted for this bullet by scope.
events.object: Elliptic surfaces (as the abstract says) in which the unbounded-degree version of the inequality fails. The explicit surfaces are not described in the abstract; the explicit construction was not read.

events.what_happened: Yu Yasufuku, arXiv:1601.03825, 'Vojta's Conjecture on Multiple Blowups of P^2 and the abc conjecture', v1 15 January 2016, v2 23 January 2016. The abstract (as fetched) shows that Vojta's conjecture on certain rational surfaces implies a special case of the abc conjecture, and conversely; and proves Vojta's conjecture unconditionally for a similar but different family of rational surfaces.
events.delivers: Unconditional Vojta-type result for a family of rational surfaces 'similar but different' from the family where the abc equivalence holds; conditional equivalence with abc on the first family.
events.remains: The stated conjecture in general (arbitrary varieties, divisors, and the full set of cases).
events.direction: Unconditional for a restricted class of rational surfaces (the analogue family), in the direction the conjecture predicts.

events.what_happened: Hector Pasten, arXiv:2205.07841, 'On the arithmetic case of Vojta's conjecture with truncated counting functions', v1 16 May 2022, v2 25 May 2022, v3 4 July 2022. The abstract (as fetched) proves a Diophantine inequality for rational points on varieties of any dimension in the direction of Vojta's conjecture with truncated counting functions, bounds the truncated counting function from below for divisors with enough components, and gives a subexponential bound toward abc in several cases. Lang-Waldschmidt is said to imply a special case of Vojta's conjecture with truncation. The fetched abstract does not contain the claim, reported in a search snippet, that this is the first unconditional result in arbitrary dimension.
events.delivers: An unconditional lower bound toward the truncated-counting-function version, for divisors with enough components, in terms of proximity to an algebraic point. The truncated version is a variant of the stated height-proximity statement.
events.remains: The non-truncated height-proximity inequality, and the general case without the components hypothesis.
events.direction: A partial unconditional result for a truncated variant, in the direction the conjecture predicts. Discounted by scope for the non-truncated statement.

No slides, notes or written version were found.
events.delivers: Not determinable: the listing gives only an abstract, and no written argument was found.
events.time_since_posted: about 15 months (talk date; no write-up found)
events.direction: Not determinable from the listing. The abstract mentions 'new observations and implications' but not whether they bear on the uniform or modified version.

events.what_happened: The ZEN Mathematics Center's LANA project (Lean for ANAbelian geometry; partners at Utrecht and Alberta; announced 31 March 2026) released an interim report on 17 July 2026 on formalising IUT. Per search snippets and press coverage (the PDF was unreadable to the fetch tool), it isolates a compatibility problem in the passage from Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 of IUT III, says the project has not reconstructed a proof of the required compatibility, and gives no final verdict on IUT. A German-language article headlined the result as 'Lean confirms gap', while the ZMC's own coverage is more cautious; Joshi's comments of 30 July 2026 dispute the methodology.
events.delivers: Nothing about Vojta's conjecture or its Vojta-type inequality. It concerns the abc route (Corollary 3.12), which is upstream of the Legendre-curve inequality claimed in joshi-2024-03.
events.revisions: Project announced 31 Mar 2026; interim report 17 Jul 2026 (dates from snippets and press coverage, not from the PDF).

checked_by.who: LANA project (Kato et al., ZEN Mathematics Center, Utrecht, Alberta)
checked_by.qualification: Lean formalisation team including arithmetic geometers, working on IUT III
checked_by.what_they_did: Attempted a Lean formalisation of the Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 step and reported an unresolved compatibility problem, with no final verdict (per secondary sources).

events.doubts: The report is interim and reports an open compatibility problem rather than a finished formalisation. The press framings differ ('Lean confirms gap' against the ZMC's more cautious position). I did not read the report.
events.direction: Interim, and cuts against the abc route's step (Corollary 3.12) as reported. It does not address the Vojta inequality specifically.

sources: Search snippets of the ZMC announcement and press coverage (not opened); no AI tool named in the snippets. The PDF was unreadable, so the report itself could not be checked for AI use.

disputes.summary: The inter-universal Teichmuller theory claims (Mochizuki's proof of abc, and the Vojta-type inequality it relies on) are disputed. Scholze and Stix (2018) said the proof has a serious gap that small modifications will not fix. Mochizuki disputes this, arguing they made impermissible simplifications. Joshi (arXiv:2403.10430, 2505.10568, and comments of 30 July 2026) defends and rebuilds the framework, and says the Scholze-Stix assertions are false. The LANA interim report (July 2026) reports an unresolved compatibility problem at Corollary 3.12 and gives no verdict. Mochizuki, Hoshi, Yamashita and Yang's April 2026 progress report argues that Lean's value for IUT is partly as a communication tool (secondary snippet, not opened). No neutral party has adjudicated the dispute in the sources I found.

Conflicting reports on whether Mochizuki's IUT papers have been accepted for publication. One press account (Nature, ScienceAlert, as quoted in a search snippet) says the roughly 600-page proof was approved for publication. A RIMS statement, as quoted in a search snippet, says the papers had not yet been accepted in a journal. The Kodai Mathematical Journal publication of Fesenko et al. (2022) is a separate, journal-published IUT paper. Not resolved here.

Whether the Legendre-curve Vojta-type inequality in arXiv:2403.10430 is a special case of the stated height-proximity conjecture, or a separate statement in the Mochizuki normalisation. The text read describes it as Vojta's Inequality in Mochizuki's sense for U_d and compactly bounded Z, not the general conjecture. It is recorded here for the judging pass; I have not decided it.

summary: No proof, disproof, or AI-attributed resolution of Vojta's height-proximity conjecture appeared in any source I could open after 26 January 2024. The main Vojta-related events in the window are: (i) Joshi's arXiv:2403.10430 (March 2024), which asserts a Vojta-type inequality for the Legendre curve over Q-bar for points of degree at most d and compactly bounded sets, and derives abc; the claim is inside the Mochizuki IUT framework, which has been disputed since 2018, and Joshi's own defences and the July 2026 LANA interim report do not settle it; (ii) partial, conditional or analogue results: Tiebekabe's arXiv:2509.05300 (August 2025) gives unconditional height bounds under a positivity hypothesis; Chen, Garcia-Fritz, Mathur and Pasten's arXiv:2602.06956 (February 2026) gives finiteness of S-integral points in many cases (a Lang-Vojta sibling); Gasbarri-Guo-Wang (January 2024), Ru-Wang (October 2024) and Morrow-Vojta (February 2025) are function-field, complex or non-Archimedean analogues; and Lehmann-McKinnon-Satriano (March 2024) is conditional on Vojta's conjecture for a different approximation statement. Neighbouring results that do not address the bullet (Gao 2025, Xie-Yuan Acta 2026, Zhou 2025) are recorded with their scope. Pre-window events are recorded too: Levin (2010) gave a counterexample to the unbounded-degree variant, Yasufuku (2016) gave an unconditional result for an analogue family of rational surfaces, Pasten (2022) gave a truncated-counting result, and Fesenko et al. (2022) gave effective versions of Mochizuki's claimed non-effective Vojta/abc/Szpiro statements. Close calls: (a) Joshi's inequality could be read as a proved special case of Vojta (the abc-type curve case) or as a restricted variant in Mochizuki's normalisation, and it rests on a contested framework; (b) Tiebekabe's gap inequality is characterised only through a third-party summary; I did not open Section 6.1. Silence: the Joshi Vojta-inequality claim has no independent reader I could find after about 31 months, though the abc claim has attracted substantial public dispute. AI: the 37 searches for AI involvement with this conjecture (named, in AI-math trackers, in announcements, and in acknowledgements) found no system credited with any Vojta result. Other problems did show AI involvement in 2026 (for example the Jacobian-conjecture counterexample credited to 'Claude Fable 5' in press and in a secondary list, and an OpenAI model's counterexample to the Erdos unit-distance conjecture). I did not research those, and none names this problem. The AI negative is limited: I could not read the full text of Joshi, Tiebekabe, Chen et al., or Gao, and I could not check acknowledgements, so 'none_found' rests on the portions read. The 2026 Sra paper 'GPT, the Counterexample Machine' (opened) names no number-theoretic conjecture beyond Erdos-type problems. Two IDs cited on the Emergent Mind open-problem page (arXiv:2603.28745 and arXiv:2608.28255) returned no results and were not opened.
competing_reading: (1) Read Joshi's arXiv:2403.10430 as a claimed proof of a special case of Vojta's conjecture: the Legendre curve with bounded-degree points is the abc-type setting, so the claimed inequality is a Vojta statement for one curve family, and a case that is 'established' in the author's view would move a restricted case of the problem. Against it: the inequality is Mochizuki's normalised version, the framework is disputed, and nobody independent has checked it. (2) Read Tiebekabe, Chen et al. and Gasbarri-Guo-Wang as real progress: each proves a substantial case of a Vojta-type statement, which the bullet's 'a case of the problem' reading would count. Against it: each is either positivity-restricted, an integral-point sibling, or a function-field analogue; the bullet asks for the number-field height-proximity inequality. (3) Read the 2010 Levin counterexample as ruling out the statement outright: Levin's unbounded-degree failure would show the bullet's literal 'algebraic points' reading is false. Against it: the bullet is over a fixed number field, and the bounded-degree statements are not refuted by that result.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The full text of arXiv:2403.10430 (Theorem 7.1.1 and the acknowledgements), a referee report or journal decision on it, and any independent expert reading of Section 7. (b) The text of Mochizuki's March 2024 report on Joshi's series and of the LANA July 2026 interim report, which I could not extract. (c) A resolution of the Corollary 3.12 step, either by a finished Lean formalisation with no sorry or by a published expert verdict. (d) The full text of arXiv:2509.05300 (Section 6.1 and Theorem 4.10), to confirm what the gap inequality covers. (e) Any published account from the ICERM talk, and any 2026 arXiv preprint on the Vojta height inequality that an arXiv full-text search for 'Vojta' would find (I used web search, not arXiv's own search). (f) For the AI question: the acknowledgements of the 2024-2026 preprints above, which I could not read in full.
